text: MCP graph parameter optional: default to the .bowman graph of the client's working directory
description:
OBSERVED 2026-11-23: every tool call needs graph=/absolute/path; in one session the agent wrote to /home/felix/life and /home/felix/dev/aimparency/v7 and guessed a full UUID wrong once. A stdio MCP inherits the client's cwd, and graph-address sessions already hide projectPath (e34b5ff1). Proposal: if graph is omitted, use the git root of the MCP process's cwd that has a .bowman; responses name which graph was used, and cross-graph calls still pass it explicitly.

Refuted if ambiguity causes wrong-graph writes; then keep it required.

status.comment: Accepted by Felix ('can we work on them?'). The stdio server now takes the graph of its working directory (graphOfDirectory in packages/mcp/src/working-graph.ts: the nearest .bowman upwards, never beyond the repository root) as the session graph. It reuses the mechanism the graph-address SSE sessions already had: tools list `graph` as optional, and the schema names which graph a call without it uses ('Leave out to work on this session's graph "…"; name another graph to work there'). Calls that name a graph still go there. A repo without a .bowman keeps `graph` required. Evidence: new working-graph.test.ts plus tools-with-accounts tests pass (4/4), mcp tsc clean, and the server starts from ~/dev/ways-of-will. Takes effect on the next /mcp reconnect. Refutation test still open: watch for writes to the wrong graph.
